inputs.userGoal: Add primary and DR deployment modes plus production and development environment modes. Production primary deploys in West Europe, production DR deploys a full stack in North Europe and geo-restores PostgreSQL from the primary server, and development always deploys in West Europe with low-cost SKUs and no Azure Front Door. Production Web Apps must only accept Azure Front Door traffic identified by the profile X-Azure-FDID header.
subGoals: Deploy production DR alongside primary in a separate novabank-prod-dr resource group.
Use AzureFrontDoor.Backend plus X-Azure-FDID App Service access restrictions instead of Private Link.
Keep development inexpensive and ignore deploymentMode=dr.

reasoning.whyChosen: Separate resource groups allow primary, DR, and dev resources with immutable regional properties to coexist.
alternativesConsidered: Same resource group with suffixed resources
reasoning.tradeoffs: Additional resource groups add lifecycle boundaries but simplify regional failover operations.

resources.name: mode-derived virtual network and private DNS

reasoning.whyChosen: Each independently deployable environment needs regional delegated subnets and PostgreSQL private DNS.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Repeated address spaces prevent direct peering without renumbering, but the environments are not peered by this scaffold.

resources.name: mode-derived PostgreSQL Flexible Server

properties.drImplementation: Native Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers resource because AVM 0.16.1 does not forward sourceServerResourceId or pointInTimeUTC for GeoRestore

reasoning.whyChosen: Production primary creates geo-redundant backups; production DR restores them into Azure's paired North Europe region; dev uses the least expensive VNet-capable Burstable SKU.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Geo-restore has nonzero RPO/RTO and must use a distinct target server name. Dev omits HA and geo backup.

dependencies: mode-derived virtual network and private DNS

resources.name: mode-derived App Service

reasoning.whyChosen: Production accepts only traffic from its own Front Door profile while dev remains directly reachable without Front Door.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Header and service-tag restrictions retain a public endpoint but prevent direct traffic that does not originate from the configured Front Door profile.

dependencies: mode-derived virtual network and private DNS

references.title: Restrict App Service to Azure Front Door

properties.originProtection: AzureFrontDoor.Backend service tag and profile-specific X-Azure-FDID

reasoning.whyChosen: Standard Front Door provides the requested routing and a profile-specific identity header without Premium Private Link cost.
alternativesConsidered: Premium Front Door with Private Link
reasoning.tradeoffs: The origin retains a public endpoint secured by access restrictions.

reasoning.whyChosen: Each environment keeps diagnostics in its own regional workspace.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Separate workspaces require cross-workspace queries for a global operational view.

overallReasoning.summary: The subscription template derives location, resource group, resource names, SKUs, Front Door deployment, and PostgreSQL create mode from deploymentMode and environmentMode. Development overrides DR requests and always deploys in West Europe.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: Geo-restore is a disaster-recovery operation rather than continuous replication. Production origin security uses public service-tag/header restrictions instead of Private Link. Globally unique Web App and Front Door endpoint names must remain available.

plan.validation: Dev ignores deploymentMode=dr; production primary and DR use separate resource groups and names; North Europe is the West Europe paired region; the DR PostgreSQL source resolves to novabank-prod/novabank-pg; Front Door is absent in dev; and production Web Apps deny traffic unless both AzureFrontDoor.Backend and the deployment-specific X-Azure-FDID match.
